# googleads_ad_group_ad (Resource)

A Responsive Search Ad under an ad group. Per the Ads API, the ad body (headlines, descriptions, URLs, paths) is immutable — Terraform replaces the resource on changes. Only status is mutable in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "googleads_ad_group_ad" "rsa" {
  customer_id = "1234567890"
  ad_group_id = googleads_ad_group.main.id
  status      = "ENABLED"

  final_urls = ["https://example.com"]

  headlines = [
    "Discover great products",
    "Shop the latest deals",
    "Free shipping over $50",
  ]

  descriptions = [
    "Curated picks updated daily.",
    "Loved by 10,000+ customers.",
  ]

  path1 = "deals"
  path2 = "today"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ad_group_id` (String) Ad group resource name.
- `customer_id` (String) Google Ads customer ID.
- `descriptions` (List of String) 2–4 description strings, each ≤90 characters.
- `final_urls` (List of String) At least one landing URL.
- `headlines` (List of String) 3–15 headline strings, each ≤30 characters.

### Optional

- `path1` (String) Optional display URL path, ≤15 characters.
- `path2` (String) Optional second display URL path, ≤15 characters. Only valid when path1 is set.
- `removal_policy` (String) Controls what happens when Terraform plans to destroy this ad. `soft` (the default behavior when unset) calls the Ads API Remove mutation, marking it REMOVED in Ads. `protect` blocks the destroy at apply time — useful for production resources where an accidental `terraform destroy` (or removal from config) shouldn't be allowed to take them offline. To destroy a protected resource, flip the policy to `soft` and apply, or remove it manually in the Ads UI and `terraform state rm` it.
- `status` (String) ENABLED (default), PAUSED, or REMOVED.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Ad group ad resource name (customers/{cid}/adGroupAds/{ag}~{ad}).
